text:
Asha Rao: Heads up — we need to submit quota increases for us-west-2 ahead of the Summer product promo (target week of Aug 11). Forecast shows a need for ~24 additional A100 instances for the Dedicated pool for a 48h burst window.

Connor Li: ✅ FYI what's the instance family and AMI constraints? are we sticking with a100-80g or mixing with a10?

Asha Rao: Primary plan is 16 x a100-80g + 8 x a10 to save cost on non-latency-critical lanes. We'll keep a100s pinned to hot-realtime routes.

Priya Ghosh: Need to check account-level limits: GPU quota, ENIs per instance type, and EIP quotas. Also request higher NAT GW throughput for burst egress.

Liam Carter: I can spin up an initial request with cloud support — two things I need: billing account ID and the preferred AZ spread. Also want to request additional elastic IPs (we'll need 12) and increase for VPC subnet IPs in the private subnets.

Asha Rao: Billing: acct-987654321. AZ spread: spread across us-west-2a/b/c. Subnet IP headroom +120 IPs to be safe.

Becca Shaw: Cost callout — if we reserve 16 a100s for 48h burst, estimate ~USD 50k pre-discount. We have runbook to fallback to a10s and 4-bit quantized models if quota not approved. Document link: https://redwood-internal/drive/summer-burst-capacity.xlsx

Connor Li: Can you paste the exact Service Quota commands/requests you plan to open? I can review before you submit.

Priya Ghosh: Draft command for AWS Service Quotas (example):
```
aws service-quotas request-service-quota-increase --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-A4707C84 --desired-value 100
```
We'll need to open three requests: EC2 GPU quota, Elastic IP quota, and VPC IPs / ENI quota.

Liam Carter: Opened ticket with AWS Support: SR-4338127 — requested 24 more instances (A100/A10 mix) and 12 additional EIPs. ETA from AWS: 3–5 business days.

DevInfraBot: [automated] Created internal tracker ticket INFRA-2028 for Summer burst quota requests. Added watchers: @Asha Rao, @Priya Ghosh, @Connor Li.

Becca Shaw: Also request increasing NAT Gateway burst capacity to avoid egress throttling — shadow traffic during canary hit. Add that as a separate ticket.

Asha Rao: Agree — Priya, can you file the NAT GW request and set priority to high? We'll need approval from finance for the short-term spend.

Priya Ghosh: Filing NAT GW and subnet IP increases now, setting priority high. Tagging finance: @Becca Shaw for cost signoff.

Connor Li: Quick config notes for Dedicated autoscaler: set min_pool = baseline (current) + 8 reserved, max_pool = baseline + 40, prewarm_timeout = 600s. That gives us headroom without spinning up everything immediately.

Asha Rao: Good. Also add fallback policy to route heavy requests to cheaper model variant when pool utilization > 80%.

Becca Shaw: Finance approved a short-term burst budget of $60k, conditional on rolling back to baseline within 72h if utilization < 30%. :thumbsup:

Liam Carter: Update — AWS responded: need justification for the EIP count and AZ spread. Pasted perf runbook and risk mitigation for single-AZ failure. Waiting on their uplift decision.

Priya Ghosh: If AWS delays, we should prepare uplift via alternative regions (us-west-1) and pre-pull images there. That adds some network complexity but keeps us safe.

Asha Rao: Good plan. Action items: Liam — follow up SR daily + paste AWS replies in INFRA-2028. Priya — file NAT GW quota request and monitor. Connor — update autoscaler config and create canary route. Becca — confirm budget on tracker. I'll notify product about the plan.

Connor Li: Will do — I'll open a small canary (2 a100 + 2 a10) in us-west-2a tomorrow 09:00 PT and share results.

Asha Rao: Thanks everyone. Ping here if AWS gives a greenlight or asks for changes.

DevInfraBot: [automated] INFRA-2028 updated: SR-4338127 linked, status = pending, last_updated = 2025-07-17 14:12 UTC.
